note: Figures from outside this project, each with its source. None is computed here, and none is a project result.

shelter_intakes_2025.measure: dog and cat community intakes to US shelters and rescues in 2025
shelter_intakes_2025.source: Shelter Animals Count, 2025 Annual Data Report, released February 4, 2026
shelter_intakes_2025.caveat: a national estimate from the Shelter Animals Count model, rounded as published

returned_to_owner_2025.measure: dogs and cats returned to their owners in 2025
returned_to_owner_2025.source: Shelter Animals Count, 2025 Annual Data Report, released February 4, 2026
returned_to_owner_2025.caveat: a national estimate from the Shelter Animals Count model, rounded as published

microchip_return_to_owner_dogs.measure: share of stray dogs returned to their owners
microchip_return_to_owner_dogs.comparison_group: all stray dogs entering the participating shelters, as described by the Ohio State University release of October 11, 2009
microchip_return_to_owner_dogs.study: 53 animal shelters in 23 US states, August 2007 to March 2008, 7,704 microchipped animals
microchip_return_to_owner_dogs.primary_source: Lord LK, Ingwersen W, Gray JL, Wintz DJ. Characterization of animals with microchips entering animal shelters. J Am Vet Med Assoc. 2009;235(2):160-167. doi:10.2460/javma.235.2.160. PMID 19601734. Peer reviewed.
microchip_return_to_owner_dogs.source_of_percentages: JAVMA News (American Veterinary Medical Association), 'Pet owners, shelters, and clinics: Check the chip', August 1, 2017, citing the paper. The paper's full text was not accessible, and the PubMed abstract does not give these two percentages.
microchip_return_to_owner_dogs.abstract_check: The abstract reports owners found for 2,191 of 2,956 microchipped stray dogs (74.1%), a different measure from return to owner.
